analysis.title: AI derating continues before the US mid-term elections
key_insights: Markets are in unstable equilibrium. Brent fell 11% on hopes for US-Iran negotiations while rotation out of AI stocks continued, with the SOX semiconductor index down 3.4% on the day and down 11% over three sessions.
Apple and Palantir earnings did not reverse the downtrend in AI sectors, where growth remains strong but is slowing.

Forward P/E is down 15% from this year's peak for the SPX, 20% for the NDX and 50% for the SOX. EPS growth expectations have accelerated sharply in recent weeks, which Natixis says suggests further downside potential.
Markets focus on the US midterm elections, with a high probability of a 'blue wave' that could ultimately widen the US budget deficit.
Euro rates eased on lower oil. The 10-year Bund fell almost 3 bp to 3.29% in a bull flattening, and 60 bp of ECB hikes are priced by September 2027 despite hawkish comments from Kazimir.
The US 10-year Treasury yield fell by as much as 5 bp to 4.88%. The RBA raised its rate 25 bp to 4.85% and signaled a pause.

Energy sold off sharply. Brent's Jan contract fell 8.5% to $103.7/bbl and TTF fell 9.8% to EUR93.7/MWh as mediation continued and headlines suggested a post-midterm US attack on Iran was less likely. Positions remain far apart and Brent was back above $107 in the morning.

Apple Q4-26 revenue rose 12% y/y to $114.5bn against $113.5bn consensus, with EPS of $2.10 against $2.00. China revenue of $17.5bn missed the $18.75bn expectation. Q1-27 revenue growth guidance of 7%-10% compares with 6.1% consensus, yet the shares fell 3.9% after hours.
Alstom issued a profit warning, cutting its adjusted EBIT margin forecast to 1%. Its 5-year CDS widened 26bp and the shares fell 26%.

Alphabet issued EUR6bn in seven tranches with 20-25bp new issue premiums, repricing its existing euro bonds about 20bp wider. Meta Platforms plans euro senior unsecured bonds on top of five planned dollar tranches.
Ryanair hedged only 25% of FY28 fuel at $95/bbl versus 80% at $67/bbl for FY27, expects up to EUR2bn of excess costs and has no Q4 visibility.
The October ISM Manufacturing Index was 55.5 against 54.5 consensus. Prices paid fell to 75.2 against 77.2 consensus.

market_movers.rationale: Q4-26 beat on revenue, iPhone and EPS, with Q1-27 guidance above consensus. Shares still fell 3.9% after hours. China revenue and gross margin (helped by tariff refunds, hurt by memory costs) were weak spots.

sector_views.rationale: The SOX fell 3.4% in a day and 11% in three sessions, and its forward P/E is down 50% from this year's peak.

earnings_insights: Apple Q4-26 (reported after the 11/2 close): revenue $114.5bn, +12% y/y, vs consensus $113.5bn. EPS $2.10 reported vs Street estimate $2.00. iPhone $57.6bn vs $56.5bn expected. China $17.5bn vs $18.75bn expected. Services $31.6bn, in line with forecasts. Q1-27 revenue growth guidance of 7%-10% vs 6.1% consensus.
Ryanair Q2-2027: H1 revenue +3%, operating costs +10% y/y in Q2 and H1, average fares -4% in H1. Only 25% of FY28 fuel is hedged at $95/bbl, with excess costs expected to reach EUR2bn.
Alstom issued a profit warning and lowered its adjusted EBIT margin forecast to 1% for this year.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 77.2 consensus and down from 77.9.
The RBA raised 25 bp and signaled a pause, with the Australian 2-year yield down 6 bp.
Market pricing moderated on lower oil despite hawkish comments from Kazimir.
Fell as much as 5 bp as oil dropped.
Fell almost 3 bp in a bull flattening.

risk_factors: Further equity derating, since EPS growth expectations have risen sharply.
A larger US budget deficit following a blue wave in the midterms.
Renewed US escalation against Iran after the midterms.
French political risk, with the OAT-Bund spread at 161 bp.
Higher fuel costs for airlines with thin hedging, such as Ryanair.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures at 20.9, up 1.9 points over five days.
Rotation out of AI stocks continues, with the SOX down 11% over three sessions.
geopolitical: Hopes for US-Iran negotiations pushed Brent down. Reports said Trump was not in a hurry and rebuffed Netanyahu's attempts to restart the war quickly, and that Iran's Supreme Leader gave the government authority for talks.
Iran sticks to its seven conditions while the US demands nuclear concessions upfront, so positions remain far apart.
The US is reportedly pushing to restart Russian gas transit via Ukraine as part of US-Ukraine-Russia talks later this month. Natixis views this as unlikely.
US midterm elections on the day of publication, with a high probability of a blue wave.

tension_points.bull_case: AI sector growth remains globally strong, and Apple beat on revenue, iPhone and EPS with guidance above consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is slowing, rotation out of AI continues, and forward P/E multiples are down 15% (SPX), 20% (NDX) and 50% (SOX). Rising EPS growth expectations leave room for further downside.
